items.text: A man committed armed robbery at 19 and served 15 years. He's now 45, has earned a degree, mentors youth, and hasn't reoffended. Has he fundamentally changed?

options.A: Yes—people can genuinely transform who they are at their core
options.B: Probably yes—most people can genuinely change with sustained effort
options.C: Uncertain—behavior changed but core nature is hard to assess
options.D: Probably not—his underlying nature is controlled, not eliminated
options.E: No—fundamental character is fixed; he's managing, not changing

items.text: Which statement about personality change is most accurate?

options.A: People can genuinely transform who they are at their core
options.B: Significant personality change is possible but requires major effort
options.C: People can change their behavior but not their fundamental nature
options.D: Personality traits are mostly fixed by early adulthood
options.E: Character is essentially permanent—"a leopard cannot change its spots"

items.text: Someone's partner has cheated three times but promises they've truly changed. The most realistic assessment is:

options.A: People can and do change—this deserves a genuine chance
options.B: Change is possible if they're genuinely committed
options.C: Past behavior is informative but not determinative
options.D: Patterns of behavior are hard to break—be cautious
options.E: Serial cheating reveals fixed character—they won't change
